title: Days Since Last Order per Customer
description: For each customer, calculate the **date of their most recent order** and the **number of days elapsed since that order** (as of a reference date '2026-03-31'). Order results from least recently active to most recently active.
solution_sql: SELECT customer_id, MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date, '2026-03-31'::DATE - MAX(order_date) AS days_since_last_order FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY days_since_last_order DESC

test_cases.description: 5 customers each with last order date and days since. C3 most dormant (last ordered Jan 8 = 82 days), C4 most recent (Mar 28 = 3 days).

hints: Use MAX(order_date) per customer to find their most recent order, then subtract from a fixed reference date to get days elapsed.
Subtracting a DATE from another DATE in PostgreSQL returns an integer number of days — no need for DATEDIFF.
explanation: MAX(order_date) within GROUP BY customer_id gives each customer's latest purchase. Subtracting from '2026-03-31' (reference date) gives the recency in days. C3: last=Jan 8, 82 days (most dormant). C2: last=Feb 8, 51 days. C5: last=Feb 22, 37 days. C1: last=Mar 20, 11 days. C4: last=Mar 28, 3 days (most recent). This recency metric is the 'R' in RFM analysis.
